title: fix(metadata-admin): the schema-driven condition editor lints in the scope its host declares (objectui#8167)
body:
Fixes #8167

Clause-②: yes

The last arm of this card: the schema-driven condition editor now lints in the scope its HOST declares, and the generic editor derives that per metadata type from a pinned table. Implements the director ruling of 2026-09-17 (batch #150 item 5, letter **B with the derivation table**, maintainer 「同意」) verbatim.

## What ships

- `WidgetContext.conditionScope: 'record' | 'flattened' | 'none'` — **required** at construction, so a host that does not decide does not compile. Compile-enforced at both non-test construction sites.
- `ConditionWidget` reads it: `record` / `flattened` reach `ConditionBuilder`'s existing `scope` prop; `none` routes the field to the plain string editor with no lint claim at all (option D, per row).
- `ResourceEditPage` — the generic editor for every metadata type — derives the value from the type being edited, through the ruled table in the new `conditionScope.ts`. It does not hard-code a value, which is what the ruling refused by name.
- `ViewVariantInspector` — the second construction site — states `none`, with the reading recorded at the site (below).
- A pin test enumerates the table against the registry of metadata resources, so a new type is a RED test rather than a silent `none`.

## The ruled table, as the ruling spells it

| metadata type | conditionScope |
| :-- | :-- |
| action (`visible` / `disabled` / `enabled`) | `record` |
| validation rule (`condition`) | `record` |
| hook (`condition`) | `record` |
| flow node (`condition`) | `flattened` |
| permission / RLS row condition | `flattened` |
| page block (`visibleWhen`) | `none` |
| any type without a row | `none` |

The page-block row is `none` NOW and this card does not wait on objectstack#18554 — the ruling says so explicitly, and the reason the page-block tier has no lint scope is already recorded at that mount and pinned by `ConditionBuilder.mountScope.test.tsx`.

## The second construction site

`ViewVariantInspector` edits a view VARIANT body. `view` is one of the ruling's "any type without a row" types, so the table's verdict is `none` — and the surface reads the same way independently: the one predicate-bearing key a variant carries is `conditionalFormatting[].condition`, and that key is authored by the curated `ConditionalFormattingEditor` mounted directly above the generic form, which declares `scope="record"` at its own mount (objectui#8164). The generic form has no surface of its own to claim, and `none` states that rather than letting `flattened` answer by default.

## An absent `WidgetContext` is unchanged

`WidgetProps.context` is optional and many in-tree `SchemaForm` mounts pass no `widgetContext` at all. Those are untouched: the widget forwards no scope, so `celAuthoring`'s `hint.scope ?? 'flattened'` answers exactly what it answered before this member existed. Treating absence as `none` would have swapped the editor under hosts nobody ruled on. There is a pin for this arm, and `SchemaForm.widgetLabelling.test.tsx`'s `condition` case (which passes no ctx) is a second, pre-existing witness that it did not move.

## Clause ② — `yes`, re-derived, and this time against the EMITTED declarations

The inherited reading was taken from source only; the prior seat said in as many words that it did not read `dist`. Re-derived here on a real build of `@object-ui/app-shell`:

| probe | reading |
| :-- | :-- |
| `WidgetContext` named in `dist/index.d.ts` | **0** |
| control — `^export` lines in `src/index.ts` | **84** (the zero is not a dead entry) |
| control — `metadata-admin` mentions in `src/index.ts` | **25**, and `SchemaForm` is exported by name (the zero is not "this directory is never exported") |
| `widgetContext?: WidgetContext` positions in `SchemaForm.tsx` | **8** |
| the emitted declaration | `dist/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.d.ts` imports the type from `./widgets.js` and declares `widgetContext?: WidgetContext` on the published props |
| package contract | not private; `files` ships `dist`; `exports["."].types` is `./dist/index.d.ts` |

So the type reaches the published `.d.ts` transitively, through an exported symbol's signature, without ever being re-exported by name.

**Proved by a real consumer compile**, not by reading: a scratch `.tsx` inside a package that links `@object-ui/app-shell`, resolving through the package name (hence through `exports.types`), built against the rebuilt `dist`:

- omitting the member ⇒ `error TS2741: Property 'conditionScope' is missing in type … but required in type 'WidgetContext'` (exit 2) — the consumer break;
- supplying it ⇒ exit 0 — the control that proves the probe can pass.

The probe file was deleted; `git status` is clean.

⇒ changeset is `@object-ui/app-shell` **minor** with the break spelled out (this repo forbids `major` in a changeset — the fixed group tracks `@objectstack`'s major).

## Verification

**New pin** `ConditionWidget.conditionScope.test.tsx` — real `@objectstack/formula`, no stub. 11 cases: the `record` arm rejects the bare shorthand and names the `record.FIELD` fix and still accepts the canonical spelling; the `flattened` arm still ACCEPTS the bare shorthand (the half that stops this from being a sweep); the `none` arm renders no builder, round-trips what is typed and keeps the `group` labelling contract; the no-context control is unchanged; and four table cases.

**Ablation — three legs, each direction predicted before running**, through `ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor must hit; on-disk before/after occurrence counts and blob hashes; restore proved by blob == HEAD and an EMPTY `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code). The fix was committed first.

| leg | mutation | predicted | observed |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| A — the wiring | drop `scope={conditionScope}` from the widget | RED, the `record` reject case | `Tests: 1 failed, 10 passed`, failing case exactly that one, failure mode the DEFECT itself (`aria-invalid` null, `Valid CEL` on screen — the bare predicate linting clean) |
| B — the `none` route | make the `none` branch unreachable | RED, the three `none` cases | `Tests: 3 failed, 8 passed`, exactly those three |
| C — the table | flip the ruled `action` row to `flattened` | RED, the ruled-verdict case | `Tests: 1 failed, 10 passed`, exactly that case |

No dist involvement in any leg: the mutated files are app-shell's own source, imported relatively by the test.

**Affected tests** — the 94 test files naming any changed subject (`WidgetContext`, `ConditionWidget`, `conditionScope`, `ResourceEditPage`, `ViewVariantInspector`, `SchemaForm`, `WIDGETS`), enumerated with `git grep -lw` (word boundary, plus a lit control at 7 files and a negative control at 0): **`Test Files 94 passed (94)` / `Tests 1596 passed (1596)`**, through the shared verify lock, verdict read from its own `VERDICT command-exit 0` line.

**Type check** — `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (the script echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test files are covered): exit 0, zero `error TS` lines. The first run was the measurement that enumerated the construction sites: **52 errors across 9 test files**, every one of them a `WidgetContext` literal.

**Lint** — `eslint packages/app-shell --format json`: exit 0, **1174 files, 0 errors**, 3031 warnings, counts read from the JSON rather than estimated. Every warning on a changed file is pre-existing: intersecting the warning lines with this diff's own hunk ranges mechanically gives **0 warnings inside added or changed lines**. NARROWING DECLARED with all three pieces: (1) population — `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint` over every package, and what ran is app-shell's own complete CI unit, the only package this diff touches; (2) the file and message counts come from `--format json`; (3) invariance — `eslint.config.js` configures no `projectService` and no `project:`, so no type-aware linting exists and a change inside app-shell cannot move another package's verdict.

**Derived gates** (objectui has no `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` — that script REFUSES a cross-repo answer, so the list is hand-derived from this repo's own `package.json` and `.github/workflows/`). Every exit code was captured with output redirected to a file first and `$?` read immediately after, never through a pipe. All exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (`0 new citation(s)`), `check-test-path-roots`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-drift`, `check:side-effects-array`, and `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over all six changed paths → `NOT GOVERNED — 6 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched`.

**NOT MEASURED, with the reason, never counted as green:**

- `check:new-line-citations` on its first invocation exited 2 with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — no merge base`: this checkout is SHALLOW (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is `true`). Re-run with an explicit `--base` at this branch's recorded base commit → exit 0.
- `check:readme-exports` exits 1 here because sibling packages (`plugin-timeline`, `plugin-gantt`) have no `dist` in this worktree — only app-shell's closure was built. The gate says in its own output that it refuses to skip an unbuilt package. This diff contains no README, so its population does not intersect the change; CI builds everything.
- `check:eager-closure` exits 2 with `No eager-closure report … the console was not built` — a broken gauge, not a passing budget. This diff adds one leaf module (a type, a frozen table and a lookup) to `widgets.tsx`'s import graph and no new cross-package edge, but that is an argument, not a measurement.
- Remote CI on this head: reported at local-verification close per the dispatch contract; no waiting and no polling.

## Carriers

`needs:contract-review` is the seat's to hang, moot or strip — this PR neither adds nor removes it, and reports its state as a reading instead.
